claim: Prey are under selection to minimize predation losses.
source: Prey are under selection to minimize predation losses.
evidence: This is a statement of established ecological theory about predator-prey dynamics.

claim: Many aquatic prey use chemical cues released by predators to initiate predator avoidance.
source: In aquatic environments, many prey use chemical cues released by predators, which initiate predator avoidance.
evidence: This is a general statement supported by established scientific knowledge in aquatic ecology.

claim: Diel vertical migration (DVM) in Daphnia spp. is induced by chemical cues (kairomones) released by planktivorous fish.
source: A prominent example of behavioral predator-avoidance constitutes diel vertical migration (DVM) in the freshwater microcrustacean Daphnia spp., which is induced by chemical cues (kairomones) released by planktivorous fish.
evidence: This is a well-established finding in the literature, referenced throughout the manuscript.

claim: 5α-cyprinol sulfate was identified as the kairomone from fish incubation water that induces DVM in Daphnia.
source: In a bioassay-guided approach using liquid chromatography and mass spectrometry, we identified the kairomone from fish incubation water as 5α-cyprinol sulfate inducing DVM in Daphnia at picomolar concentrations.
evidence: This is the primary finding of the study, supported by experimental data from bioassays and chemical analysis.

claim: 5α-cyprinol sulfate induces DVM in Daphnia at picomolar concentrations.
source: In a bioassay-guided approach using liquid chromatography and mass spectrometry, we identified the kairomone from fish incubation water as 5α-cyprinol sulfate inducing DVM in Daphnia at picomolar concentrations.
evidence: This is supported by dose-response experimental data shown in Figure 4.

claim: 5α-cyprinol sulfate plays a role in lipid digestion in fish.
source: The role of 5α-cyprinol sulfate in lipid digestion in fish explains why from an evolutionary perspective fish has not stopped releasing 5α-cyprinol sulfate despite the disadvantages for the releaser.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about bile salt function in vertebrates.

claim: Fish have not stopped releasing 5α-cyprinol sulfate despite disadvantages because of its role in lipid digestion.
source: The role of 5α-cyprinol sulfate in lipid digestion in fish explains why from an evolutionary perspective fish has not stopped releasing 5α-cyprinol sulfate despite the disadvantages for the releaser.
evidence: This is an inference based on the essential metabolic function of bile salts.

claim: Predation is an important selective force that drives the shape of trophic cascades and numerous aspects of ecosystem ecology.
source: Predation is recognized as an important selective force which has been shown to drive the shape of trophic cascades and numerous aspects of ecosystem ecology (Gliwicz, 1986; Lima, 1998; Werner and Peacor, 2003).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Effects of predators are caused by direct predation (consumptive effect) or by effects on plastic traits of prey seeking to avoid predation (non-consumptive effect).
source: Such effects of predators are caused by predation (direct consumptive effect; Preisser et al., 2005) or by effects on plastic behavioral, physiological or morphological traits of prey seeking to avoid predation (indirect, non-consumptive effect, (Heithaus et al., 2008; Lima, 1998; Moll et al., 2017; Werner and Peacor, 2003).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Non-consumptive predator effects strongly affect prey distribution, demography and behavior.
source: It has become clear that non-consumptive predator effects strongly affect prey distribution, demography and behavior (Heithaus et al., 2008; Lima, 1998; Werner and Peacor, 2003) and the strength of top-down and bottom-up control in communities (Ford et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: In aquatic food webs, non-consumptive effects exceed direct consumptive effects.
source: Hence, non-consumptive predator effects are mediated by shifts in plastic traits of prey, and in aquatic food webs such non-consumptive effects exceed direct consumptive effects (Preisser et al., 2005; Turner et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Chemical cues are superior to physical contact and vision in turbid or dark environments.
source: Chemical cues are superior cues in turbid or dark environments (Kats and Dill, 1998) or in cases in which the escape capability upon attack is low in prey, for example due to low escape velocity.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: The induction of defenses by chemical cues from predators is widespread in aquatic systems.
source: In line with this, the induction of defenses by chemical cues from predators is widespread in aquatic systems (Bjærke et al., 2014; Brönmark and Hansson, 2012), and recently progress has been made by identification of chemical cues involved in aquatic predator-prey chemical communication (Poulin et al., 2018; Selander et al., 2015; Weiss et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Daphnia play a key role in lakes and ponds as major consumers of planktonic primary producers and important prey for higher trophic levels.
source: One classical example of behavioral predator avoidance is diel vertical migration (DVM) in the freshwater microcrustacean Daphnia, which play a key role in lakes and ponds, as they are major consumers of planktonic primary producers and important prey for higher trophic levels (Miner et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: DVM is a widespread predator avoidance behavior.
source: DVM is a widespread predator avoidance behavior (Hays, 2003; Williamson et al., 2011), in which the exposure to UV (Rhode et al., 2001) and the risk of predation by visually oriented predators, such as fish, is reduced by daytime residence in the dark, deep layer of the water column (Hays, 2003; Stich and Lampert, 1981).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: DVM reduces exposure to UV and the risk of predation by visually oriented predators through daytime residence in the dark, deep layer of the water column.
source: DVM is a widespread predator avoidance behavior (Hays, 2003; Williamson et al., 2011), in which the exposure to UV (Rhode et al., 2001) and the risk of predation by visually oriented predators, such as fish, is reduced by daytime residence in the dark, deep layer of the water column (Hays, 2003; Stich and Lampert, 1981).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: At night, zooplankton emerges from the depth into the upper water layer to minimize demographic costs associated with residence in the cold, food-depleted deep-water refuge.
source: At night, zooplankton emerges from the depth into the upper water layer to minimize demographic costs associated with residence in the cold, food-depleted deep-water refuge (Loose and Dawidowicz, 1994; Stich and Lampert, 1981).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: DVM of Daphnia negatively affects the foraging success of planktivorous fish.
source: Hence, DVM of Daphnia negatively affects the foraging success of planktivorous fish.
evidence: This is an inference based on the behavior of Daphnia avoiding fish during the day.

claim: DVM affects the control of planktonic primary producers by zooplankton and impacts many ecosystem-wide processes.
source: This behavioral anti-predator defense affects the control of planktonic primary producers by zooplankton in the open water and thus impacts many other ecosystem-wide processes (Haupt et al., 2010; Reichwaldt and Stibor, 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: DVM in zooplankton is triggered by changes in light intensity and by chemical cues released by predators.
source: In lakes and ponds, DVM in zooplankton is triggered by changes in light intensity (Effertz and von Elert, 2014; Ringelberg, 1999) and by chemical cues released by predators (Dodson, 1988; Lampert, 1993; Neill, 1990).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: The amplitude of DVM increases with fish density.
source: The finding that the amplitude of DVM increases with fish density indicates that kairomones provide a reliable indicator for the risk of Daphnia of being preyed upon by fish (Van Gool and Ringelberg, 2002; von Elert and Pohnert, 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Kairomones provide a reliable indicator for the risk of Daphnia of being preyed upon by fish.
source: The finding that the amplitude of DVM increases with fish density indicates that kairomones provide a reliable indicator for the risk of Daphnia of being preyed upon by fish (Van Gool and Ringelberg, 2002; von Elert and Pohnert, 2000).
evidence: This is an inference based on the correlation between fish density and DVM amplitude, supported by citations.

claim: Fish-Daphnia interactions are largely determined by indirect, non-consumptive effects of fish mediated by kairomones inducing predator avoidance by DVM.
source: Thus, fish - Daphnia interactions are to a large degree determined by indirect, non-consumptive effects of fish that are mediated by kairomones inducing predator avoidance by DVM.
evidence: This is an inference based on the established role of kairomones in inducing DVM.

claim: The release of the DVM-inducing kairomone does not depend on prior feeding of fish.
source: Earlier we have shown that the release of the DVM-inducing kairomone does not depend on prior feeding of fish (Loose et al., 1993).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research by the authors.

claim: The kairomone can be extracted from fish incubation water by lipophilic solid phase extraction.
source: The kairomone can be extracted from fish incubation water by lipophilic solid phase extraction, and we have characterized it as a low molecular weight compound carrying a hydroxyl group and a negative charge (Loose et al., 1993; von Elert and Pohnert, 2000; von Elert and Loose, 1996).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research by the authors.

claim: The kairomone is a low molecular weight compound carrying a hydroxyl group and a negative charge.
source: The kairomone can be extracted from fish incubation water by lipophilic solid phase extraction, and we have characterized it as a low molecular weight compound carrying a hydroxyl group and a negative charge (Loose et al., 1993; von Elert and Pohnert, 2000; von Elert and Loose, 1996).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research by the authors.

claim: Extract of fish incubation water (EFI) induced a significant shift in the daytime residence depth of Daphnia.
source: EFI was found to be active, as it induced a significant shift in the daytime residence depth of Daphnia.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Only fraction three from HPLC fractionation of EFI induced DVM.
source: Fractionation of EFI by HPLC yielded six fractions (Figure 1A), of which only fraction three proved to induce DVM (Figure 1B, Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1B and the associated source data.

claim: The most abundant ion in the active fraction three had a m/z of 531.29993 corresponding to the deprotonated molecule [M– H]–.
source: Mass data extracted from the time window corresponding to the active fraction 3 (11–14 min), indicated that in this active fraction the most abundant ion had a m/z of 531.29993 corresponding to the deprotonated molecule [M– H]–, which led to Mcalc. = m/z 532.3070 (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Collision-induced fragmentation of [M– H]– resulted in a product ion with a mass of m/z 96.95996 corresponding to hydrogen sulfate (HSO4–), indicating the presence of a sulfate group.
source: The collision-induced fragmentation of [M– H]– resulted in the detection of the precursor ion and a product ion with a mass of m/z 96.95996 (Figure 2B) corresponding to the monoisotopic mass of hydrogen sulfate (HSO4–calc=m/z 96.96010, ∆ = –1.44 ppm), thus indicating the presence of a sulfate group.
evidence: This is supported by MS-MS data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The predicted sum formula for [M-H]- was C27H48O8S.
source: The predicted sum formula for [M-H]- was C27H48O8S.
evidence: This is based on computational analysis of mass spectrometry data using MassWorks software.

claim: A database search yielded cyprinol sulfate (CPS) as the best hit candidate compound for the DVM-inducing activity.
source: A data base search using the platform PubChem yielded as best hit cyprinol sulfate (CPS), a known bile compound of fish (Hagey et al., 2010), as a candidate compound for the DVM-inducing activity.
evidence: This is based on database search results and supported by a citation.

claim: Cyprinol sulfate is a known bile compound of fish.
source: A data base search using the platform PubChem yielded as best hit cyprinol sulfate (CPS), a known bile compound of fish (Hagey et al., 2010), as a candidate compound for the DVM-inducing activity.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Taurochenodeoxycholic acid (TCDCA) was present in the active fraction three.
source: Subsequent search for other known bile compounds of fish in the active fraction three revealed the presence of taurochenodeoxycholic acid (TCDCA, Figure 2A, insert, [M-H]-=m/z 498.28981, C24H44NO6S, Mcalc = m/z 499.28981, ∆=1.8 ppm).
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Dilutions of extracted bile of carp and trout corresponding to similar CPS concentrations as found in EFI induced DVM with amplitudes statistically not distinguishable from those induced by EFI.
source: Dilutions of extracted bile of both species corresponding to similar CPS concentrations as found in EFI (carp: 1 and 2 nM, trout: 0.4 and 3.9 nM, EFI: 1 nM) proved to induce DVM with amplitudes that were statistically not distinguishable from those induced by EFI (Figure 3—figure supplement 2 and Figure 3—figure supplement 2—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: α-CPS and TCDCA were present in carp bile and trout bile with identical retention times, high-resolution m/z ratios and fragmentation patterns after MS-MS as in EFI.
source: When we compared chromatograms of EFI and the fish bile samples, identical retention times, high-resolution m/z ratios and fragmentation patterns after MS-MS confirmed that α-CPS and TCDCA were also present in carp bile and trout bile (Figure 3, Figure 3—figure supplements 1 and 2).
evidence: This is supported by chromatographic and mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 3 and its supplements.

claim: 5α-cyprinol sulfate (α-CPS) constitutes the major bile compound in cyprinid fish.
source: It is well known, that 5α-cyprinol sulfate (α-CPS) constitutes the major bile compound in cyprinid fish (Hagey et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: The structure of α-CPS isolated from common carp gallbladder was determined by NMR in a previous study.
source: Since it is not commercially available, we have isolated α-CPS on a semi-preparative scale from gallbladder of common carp (Cyprinidae) and determined its structure by NMR to be α-CPS in a previous study (Hahn et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research by the authors.

claim: The major constituent of the only active fraction in EFI was the bile salt α-CPS.
source: We conclude that the major constituent of the only active fraction in EFI was the bile salt α-CPS.
evidence: This is an inference based on the combined chromatographic, mass spectrometry, and bioassay data.

claim: α-CPS induced DVM at concentrations ≥ 100 pM.
source: α-CPS induced the same predator-avoidance behavior as extracted fish incubation water (EFI) at concentrations ≥ 100 pM (Figur 4A, Figure 4—source data 2).
evidence: This is supported by dose-response experimental data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: TCDCA was active at ≥20 µM only.
source: TCDCA proved to be active at ≥20 µM only (Figure 4B, Figure 4—source data 3).
evidence: This is supported by dose-response experimental data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Chenodeoxycholic acid (CDCA) was inactive with respect to DVM-induction in concentrations ≤ 25 µM.
source: As a possible microbial degradation product of TCDCA , we further tested chenodeoxycholic acid (Shimada et al., 1969) which proved to be inactive with respect to DVM-induction in concentrations ≤ 25 µM (Figure 4C, Figure 4—source data 4).
evidence: This is supported by dose-response experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Daphnia were five orders of magnitude more sensitive to α-CPS than to TCDCA.
source: In other words, Daphnia were five orders of magnitude more sensitive to α-CPS than to TCDCA, while no DVM induction was found in response to chenodeoxycholic acid (CDCA), the deconjugated form of TCDCA.
evidence: This is an inference based on the comparison of threshold concentrations from dose-response experiments.

claim: The actual concentration of α-CPS in biologically active water was 1.03 ± 0.08 nM.
source: The actual concentration of α-CPS in biologically active water was 1.03 ± 0.08 nM (mean ± SD, n = 3) and that of TCDCA was 0.14 ± 0.01 nM (mean ± SD, n = 3).
evidence: This is based on quantification of α-CPS in EFI using LC-MS.

claim: The concentration of TCDCA in biologically active water was 0.14 ± 0.01 nM.
source: The actual concentration of α-CPS in biologically active water was 1.03 ± 0.08 nM (mean ± SD, n = 3) and that of TCDCA was 0.14 ± 0.01 nM (mean ± SD, n = 3).
evidence: This is based on quantification of TCDCA in EFI using LC-MS.

claim: The concentration of α-CPS was 7.5-fold higher than that of TCDCA in biologically active water.
source: Hence the concentration of α-CPS was 7.5-fold higher than that of TCDCA.
evidence: This is a calculation based on the measured concentrations of α-CPS and TCDCA.

claim: The concentration of α-CPS in biologically active water clearly exceeded the threshold concentration for biological activity of 100 pM.
source: This concentration of α-CPS in biologically active water clearly exceeded the threshold concentration for biological activity of 100 pM, whereas TCDCA was present in concentrations that were more than five orders of magnitude below the activity threshold concentration of 20 µM.
evidence: This is a comparison of measured concentration with experimentally determined threshold.

claim: TCDCA was present in concentrations more than five orders of magnitude below the activity threshold concentration of 20 µM.
source: This concentration of α-CPS in biologically active water clearly exceeded the threshold concentration for biological activity of 100 pM, whereas TCDCA was present in concentrations that were more than five orders of magnitude below the activity threshold concentration of 20 µM.
evidence: This is a comparison of measured concentration with experimentally determined threshold.

claim: α-CPS is the only tested bile salt that is relevant for the induction of DVM in Daphnia in response to fish.
source: We therefore conclude that α-CPS is the only tested bile salt that is relevant for the induction of DVM in Daphnia in response to fish.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the combined data showing α-CPS is present at active concentrations while TCDCA is not.

claim: α-CPS is active at a concentration of 100 pM.
source: We show that the induction of DVM in Daphnia is dependent on a particular bile compound from fish, that is 5α-cyprinol sulfate (α-CPS), which is active already at a concentration of 100 pM.
evidence: This is supported by dose-response experimental data.

claim: α-CPS constitutes the major activity in fish incubation water.
source: The identification of α-CPS is the result of a bioassay-guided approach in which we have targeted the main activity throughout all purification steps. Hence, α-CPS constitutes the major activity in fish incubation water.
evidence: This is an inference based on the bioassay-guided fractionation approach.

claim: Only α-CPS was present in sufficiently high concentrations to be biologically active.
source: Although another bile compound (TCDCA) was found in the active fraction obtained by HPLC, only α-CPS was present in sufficiently high concentrations to be biologically active.
evidence: This is based on comparison of measured concentrations with threshold concentrations.

claim: Daphnia is five orders of magnitude more sensitive to α-CPS than to TCDCA.
source: This is due to two factors: (i) Daphnia is five orders of magnitude more sensitive to α-CPS than to TCDCA and (ii) the concentration of α-CPS in extracted fish incubation water is approximately sevenfold higher than that of TCDCA.
evidence: This is based on comparison of threshold concentrations from dose-response experiments.

claim: The concentration of α-CPS in extracted fish incubation water is approximately sevenfold higher than that of TCDCA.
source: This is due to two factors: (i) Daphnia is five orders of magnitude more sensitive to α-CPS than to TCDCA and (ii) the concentration of α-CPS in extracted fish incubation water is approximately sevenfold higher than that of TCDCA.
evidence: This is based on quantification of both compounds in EFI.

claim: The substantially higher concentration of α-CPS is in accordance with findings that α-CPS constitutes the major bile salt in cyprinid bile.
source: This substantially higher concentration of α-CPS is well in accordance with the findings that α-CPS constitutes the major bile salt in cyprinid bile (Hofmann et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: α-CPS matches the previously published chemical characteristics for the DVM-inducing fish kairomone of roach and other cyprinid fishes.
source: α-CPS matches perfectly the previously published chemical characteristics for the DVM-inducing fish kairomone of roach (Rutilus rutilus) and other cyprinid fishes (Loose et al., 1993; von Elert and Loose, 1996).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research by the authors.

claim: The molecular mass of α-CPS is close to 500 Dalton.
source: Its molecular mass is close to 500 Dalton, it contains hydroxyl and no amino groups, has a strong negative charge and, as predicted, α-CPS is free of olefinic bonds.
evidence: This is based on the mass spectrometry data showing the molecular mass.

claim: α-CPS contains hydroxyl groups and no amino groups.
source: Its molecular mass is close to 500 Dalton, it contains hydroxyl and no amino groups, has a strong negative charge and, as predicted, α-CPS is free of olefinic bonds.
evidence: This is based on the chemical structure determined by NMR and MS-MS data.

claim: α-CPS has a strong negative charge.
source: Its molecular mass is close to 500 Dalton, it contains hydroxyl and no amino groups, has a strong negative charge and, as predicted, α-CPS is free of olefinic bonds.
evidence: This is based on the presence of the sulfate group detected by MS-MS.

claim: α-CPS is free of olefinic bonds.
source: Its molecular mass is close to 500 Dalton, it contains hydroxyl and no amino groups, has a strong negative charge and, as predicted, α-CPS is free of olefinic bonds.
evidence: This is based on the chemical structure determined by NMR.

claim: The anionic character and hydroxyl groups make α-CPS a good infochemical in water by rendering it water soluble.
source: The anionic character and the hydroxyl groups make α-CPS a good infochemical in water, as they render the molecule water soluble so that it can well diffuse after release by the predator.
evidence: This is an inference based on chemical properties and their functional implications.

claim: Bile salts have the primary function to emulsify dietary fats and facilitate their intestinal absorption.
source: α-CPS, a sulfated bile alcohol, belongs to the bile salts, which are metabolites of cholesterol in vertebrates with the primary function to emulsify dietary fats and to facilitate their intestinal absorption (Maldonado-Valderrama et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Fish excrete bile salts via the intestine, the gills and the urinary tract.
source: Although bile salts are an essential component of the enterohepatic circulation, fish excrete bile salts via the intestine, the gills and the urinary tract (Buchinger et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Excreted fish bile salts are often highly water soluble due to conjugation with a sulfate or with taurine.
source: Excreted fish bile salts are often highly water soluble due to conjugation with a sulfate (in case of bile alcohols), or with taurine (in case of bile acids).
evidence: This is based on established knowledge of bile salt chemistry.

claim: Bile salts are generally stable as they must be resistant to digestion within an organism.
source: Furthermore, bile salts are generally stable as they must be resistant to digestion within an organism, which makes conjugated bile salts ideal infochemicals.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge of bile salt function.

claim: Conjugated bile salts are ideal infochemicals due to their stability.
source: Furthermore, bile salts are generally stable as they must be resistant to digestion within an organism, which makes conjugated bile salts ideal infochemicals.
evidence: This is an inference based on the stability property of bile salts.

claim: The induction of DVM by fish does not require successful hunting of fish.
source: Corroborating results for other bile salts (Zhang et al., 2001), we here demonstrate the release of α-CPS by starved fish. Hence, the induction of DVM by fish does not require successful hunting of fish.
evidence: This is an inference based on the demonstration that starved fish release α-CPS.

claim: Bile salts are essential in fish metabolism.
source: The fact that bile salts are essential in fish metabolism explains why, from an evolutionary perspective, fish have not stopped to release bile salts despite its disadvantage for the emitter organism.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge of bile salt function in vertebrate metabolism.

claim: Fish have not stopped releasing bile salts despite disadvantages because bile salts are essential in fish metabolism.
source: The fact that bile salts are essential in fish metabolism explains why, from an evolutionary perspective, fish have not stopped to release bile salts despite its disadvantage for the emitter organism.
evidence: This is an inference based on the essential metabolic function of bile salts.

claim: The DVM-inducing kairomone identified is the first identification of an aquatic kairomone that mediates predator-prey interactions between zooplankton and fish.
source: The DVM-inducing kairomone that we report here is to our knowledge the first identification of an aquatic kairomone that mediates predator-prey interactions between zooplankton and fish.
evidence: This is a claim about the novelty of the finding, based on the authors' knowledge of the literature.

claim: Copepods release copepodamides, which lead to increased toxicity in their dinoflagellate prey.
source: Copepods were shown to release copepodamides, a class of taurine containing polar lipids, which leads to an increased toxicity in their dinoflagellate prey (Selander et al., 2015);
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Daphnia release an alkylsulfate that induces the formation of protective colonies in the green alga Acutodesmus obliquus.
source: Daphnia have been reported to release an alkylsulfate into the water that induces the formation of protective colonies in the green alga Acutodesmus obliquus (Uchida et al., 2008),
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Larvae of Chaoborus sp. release fatty acids bound to a particular amino acid, which lead to changes in morphology in Daphnia pulex.
source: larvae of Chaoborus sp. release fatty acids bound to a particular amino acid, which lead to changes in morphology in Daphnia pulex (Weiss et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: A predatory crab releases two pyridin-metabolites that induce defensive behavior in a prey crab.
source: Among benthic animals a predatory crab has been shown to release two pyridin-metabolites that induce defensive behavior in a prey crab (Poulin et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: The sterane core of α-CPS renders it partly lipophilic.
source: The sterane core of α-CPS renders it partly lipophilic, and causes together with the sulfate group the overall amphipathic nature of α-CPS.
evidence: This is based on knowledge of the chemical structure and properties of steranes.

claim: The sterane core and sulfate group together cause the overall amphipathic nature of α-CPS.
source: The sterane core of α-CPS renders it partly lipophilic, and causes together with the sulfate group the overall amphipathic nature of α-CPS.
evidence: This is based on knowledge of chemical structure-property relationships.

claim: Sulfate or sulfonium groups are present in several compounds known in chemical communication of zooplankton.
source: Sulfate or sulfonium groups are present in several of the compounds known in chemical communication of zooplankton (Selander et al., 2015; Uchida et al., 2008) and as well in the sex pheromone of lamprey (Li et al., 2002).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The family of Cyprinidae is the largest family of fishes with more than 2000 species.
source: The family of Cyprinidae is with more than 2000 species the largest family of fishes, and dominates freshwater habitats around the world with the exception of South America and Australia, and a considerable number of species is found in brackish water (Hastings et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Cyprinidae dominates freshwater habitats around the world with the exception of South America and Australia.
source: The family of Cyprinidae is with more than 2000 species the largest family of fishes, and dominates freshwater habitats around the world with the exception of South America and Australia, and a considerable number of species is found in brackish water (Hastings et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Incubation water of many cyprinid species has been demonstrated to induce DVM in Daphnia.
source: In line with the high diversity of cyprinid fish, incubation water of many cyprinid species has been demonstrated to induce DVM in Daphnia (Lass and Spaak, 2003), and we have shown that the chemical characteristics of the kairomone are identical among different cyprinid species (von Elert and Loose, 1996) which matches the finding that α-CPS is the dominant bile salt in the Cypriniformes (Hagey et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The chemical characteristics of the kairomone are identical among different cyprinid species.
source: In line with the high diversity of cyprinid fish, incubation water of many cyprinid species has been demonstrated to induce DVM in Daphnia (Lass and Spaak, 2003), and we have shown that the chemical characteristics of the kairomone are identical among different cyprinid species (von Elert and Loose, 1996) which matches the finding that α-CPS is the dominant bile salt in the Cypriniformes (Hagey et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research by the authors.

claim: α-CPS is the dominant bile salt in the Cypriniformes.
source: In line with the high diversity of cyprinid fish, incubation water of many cyprinid species has been demonstrated to induce DVM in Daphnia (Lass and Spaak, 2003), and we have shown that the chemical characteristics of the kairomone are identical among different cyprinid species (von Elert and Loose, 1996) which matches the finding that α-CPS is the dominant bile salt in the Cypriniformes (Hagey et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Non-cyprinid fish species like perch, stickleback and pike induce DVM in Daphnia.
source: As well non-cyprinid fish species like perch, stickleback (Perciformes) and pike (Esociformes) induce DVM in Daphnia (von Elert and Pohnert, 2000), and the chemical characteristics of kairomones from pike and stickleback match those of cyprinids (von Elert and Pohnert, 2000), which suggests that the kairomones of non-cyprinid and cyprinid species are similar and perhaps identical.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research by the authors.

claim: The chemical characteristics of kairomones from pike and stickleback match those of cyprinids.
source: As well non-cyprinid fish species like perch, stickleback (Perciformes) and pike (Esociformes) induce DVM in Daphnia (von Elert and Pohnert, 2000), and the chemical characteristics of kairomones from pike and stickleback match those of cyprinids (von Elert and Pohnert, 2000), which suggests that the kairomones of non-cyprinid and cyprinid species are similar and perhaps identical.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research by the authors.

claim: The kairomones of non-cyprinid and cyprinid species are similar and perhaps identical.
source: As well non-cyprinid fish species like perch, stickleback (Perciformes) and pike (Esociformes) induce DVM in Daphnia (von Elert and Pohnert, 2000), and the chemical characteristics of kairomones from pike and stickleback match those of cyprinids (von Elert and Pohnert, 2000), which suggests that the kairomones of non-cyprinid and cyprinid species are similar and perhaps identical.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the similarity of chemical characteristics.

claim: α-CPS is confined to Cypriniformes and absent in the fish orders Perciformes, Esociformes and Salmoniformes according to a general pattern from comprehensive analysis of bile salt patterns in fish.
source: However, a general pattern that emerges from a comprehensive analysis of bile salt patterns in fish indicates that α-CPS is confined to Cypriniformes and absent in the fish orders Perciformes, Esociformes and Salmoniformes.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge from comprehensive bile salt analysis in fish.

claim: α-CPS is present in bile of rainbow trout (Oncorhynchus mykiss), a representative of Salmoniformes.
source: Yet, we here demonstrate the presence of α-CPS in bile of rainbow trout (Oncorhynchus mykiss), a representative of Salmoniformes.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data from LC-MS analysis of trout bile.

claim: The general bile salt pattern considers only bile salt types present at 5% or greater of the bile salt pool.
source: Still, this finding is in accordance with the general bile salt pattern in fish, as this pattern considers only bile salt types present at 5% or greater of the bile salt pool (Hagey et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: The production of bile alcohols such as α-cyprinol and their conjugation to sulfate is regarded as an evolutionarily ancient bile salt profile.
source: Furthermore, the authors argue, that the production of bile alcohols such as α-cyprinol (a C27 bile alcohol) and their conjugation to sulfate is regarded as an evolutionarily ancient bile salt profile (Hagey et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Evolutionarily more recent bile salt patterns of fish have evolved from the putatively ancestral pattern of C27 bile alcohol production by subsequent enzymatic modifications.
source: All evolutionarily more recent bile salt patterns of fish seem to have evolved from the putatively ancestral pattern of C27 bile alcohol production by subsequent enzymatic modifications of them (Hagey et al., 2010; Hofmann et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Bile of many ray-finned fish species contains traces of the biosynthetic precursor C27 bile alcohol though their bile is dominated by conjugated C24 bile acids.
source: In line with this bile of many ray-finned fish species still contains traces of the biosynthetic precursor C27 bile alcohol though their bile is dominated by conjugated C24 bile acids (Hagey et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: α-CPS may be present in traces (i.e. <5%) in fish orders with a more recent bile acid pattern.
source: We deduce that even in fish orders with a more recent bile acid pattern, α-CPS may be present in traces (i.e. <5%) as we have demonstrated for salmon, although this remains to be demonstrated for example for stickleback and Perciformes.
evidence: This is an inference based on the demonstration of α-CPS in salmon and the evolutionary pattern of bile salts.

claim: Daphnia evolution has selected for a high sensitivity to the evolutionarily oldest bile product of fish, α-CPS.
source: Our findings thus suggest that Daphnia evolution has selected for a high sensitivity to the evolutionarily oldest bile product of fish, that is α-CPS, and that this has proven to be an evolutionarily stable strategy as evolutionarily more recent fish bile patterns still contain traces of α-CPS.
evidence: This is a speculation based on the evolutionary patterns of bile salts and Daphnia sensitivity.

claim: High sensitivity to α-CPS has proven to be an evolutionarily stable strategy because evolutionarily more recent fish bile patterns still contain traces of α-CPS.
source: Our findings thus suggest that Daphnia evolution has selected for a high sensitivity to the evolutionarily oldest bile product of fish, that is α-CPS, and that this has proven to be an evolutionarily stable strategy as evolutionarily more recent fish bile patterns still contain traces of α-CPS.
evidence: This is a speculation based on evolutionary reasoning.

claim: By sensing a single bile compound only, Daphnia are able to perceive the presence of fish across very different orders.
source: Thus, by sensing a single bile compound only, Daphnia are able to perceive the presence of fish across very different orders (Hagey et al., 2010).
evidence: This is an inference based on the presence of α-CPS across different fish orders.

claim: The identification of α-CPS allows for the assessment of its in situ concentration in space and time.
source: The identification of α-CPS as the DVM-inducing kairomone in Daphnia allows for the assessment of its in situ concentration in space and time and thus to understand trait-variation in Daphnia and within-lake variations of DVM-amplitudes.
evidence: This is a speculation about future research possibilities enabled by the identification.

claim: Cessation of DVM in marine copepods in the absence of fish has been shown.
source: Still, although cessation of DVM in marine copepods in the absence of fish has been shown (Bollens and Frost, 1991), its induction in the presence of fish could not be demonstrated (Bollens and Frost, 1991).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Induction of DVM in marine copepods in the presence of fish could not be demonstrated.
source: Still, although cessation of DVM in marine copepods in the absence of fish has been shown (Bollens and Frost, 1991), its induction in the presence of fish could not be demonstrated (Bollens and Frost, 1991).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Daytime residence depth determined on day 3 of the bioassay is a function of kairomone concentrations.
source: The standardized experimental design has been shown to be a reliable indicator for the assessment of the kairomone, as the daytime depth determined on day 3 of the bioassay is a function of kairomone concentrations (Loose et al., 1993).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Controls for C18-SPE do not affect the daytime position of D. magna.
source: It has been shown earlier that controls for C18-SPE do not affect the daytime position of D. magna (von Elert and Loose, 1996).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research by the authors.

claim: Free bile acids occur in fish feces, suggesting a low degree of bacterial deconjugation of conjugated bile acids by gut bacteria.
source: The observation that free bile acids occur in fish feces suggests a low degree of bacterial deconjugation of conjugated bile acids by gut bacteria (Philipp, 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Bacterial deconjugation of TCDCA would not release DVM-inducing activity because the resulting free C24 bile acid CDCA was less active than TCDCA.
source: However, such bacterial deconjugation of TCDCA would not release DVM-inducing activity, as the resulting free C24 bile acid CDCA was even less active than TCDCA.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data showing CDCA is less active than TCDCA.

claim: The finding that α-CPS constitutes the major kairomone does not support the suggestion that bacteria are involved in the production of the kairomone.
source: Neither this finding nor the fact that α-CPS, a fish metabolite that has not been microbially modified, constitutes the major kairomone in fish incubation water support the earlier suggestion that bacteria are involved in the production of the kairomone (Ringelberg and Van Gool, 1998).
evidence: This is an inference that contradicts a prior hypothesis, based on the identification of α-CPS as an unmodified fish metabolite.

claim: The second peak in the EIC of m/z = 531.29986 at 2.38 min is speculated to be the isomer β-cyprinol sulfate.
source: While the ion detected at 2,04 min is of unknown identity (Figure 3C), we speculate that the second peak in the EIC of m/z = 531.29986 at 2.38 min (Figure 3D) is the isomer β-cyprinol sulfate.
